text:
Robert Thomas has 14 points in 20 games for St. Louis, but only three goals and 25 shots. That's the whole story: a center who Evolving-Hockey had 20th among 401 forwards in wins above replacement last season is barely shooting, and went without a shot in three of his last ten.

Three goals on 4.6 expected is a little unlucky, but the bigger gap is in the chances themselves. His points pace (2.05 per 60) is below league average for forwards, well under the 3.15 he posted last season and below his talent range.

The underlying play is fine. St. Louis takes 51.1% of the expected goals with him at five on five, a couple of points better than without him, and the Blues have scored 3.9 more goals than expected in those minutes. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his own zone with possession 79% of the time last season and setting up teammates at a 94th percentile rate. What to watch: the playmaking is still there. Our range has him around 73 points. Getting there likely takes a few more pucks headed for the net from his own stick.
headline: Robert Thomas isn't shooting, and it shows
